x: In reading his report we had a moment or two of thought for the passing of three of our club members: dear old Charlie Cook, Tom Sullivan and Rowland Rowbottom, which we all regret.
The Licensee here was Tom Sullivan - a well known man in the running world - who just before World War 1 went to Germany as Chief Rowing coach and laid the foundations of this sport in Germany.

The photograph opposite was taken outside Tom Sullivan's club room on the day of the Club '7' of 1912. Seven of the group had been, or were to become, Presidents of Belgrave Harriers; you will see from your handbook who they were.

In our last issue we printed a photograph of Club members outside Tom Sullivan's pub at Barnes, supplied by Albert Macher. For the record it should be noted that this photograph was taken in 1913 (not 1912 as stated) and in fact appeared in"LOTINGA'S Weekly" on 26th April 1913.
Tom Sullivan, in that photo, was a famous champion sculler who left England a few days after the picture was taken to coach the Berliner Ruder Club.

The Spencer Arms was being run at that time by the former British Professional Sculling champion Tom Sullivan, who left England for Germany about 1913 to coach the Berlin Rowing Club and was interned in Germany during the 1st World War.

Round about 1908 no. 180 Kings Road, Chelsea became the Club's main headquarters with cross country taking place from the "Spencer Arms" Barnes, where the licensee was a famous man in the sporting world - rowing coach Tom Sullivan.
